item.ptxt: Unless you pay adequate attention when removing the suspension arm joint from the steering knuckle, the dust cover of the suspension arm joint may be damaged by the puller.
When you remove the suspension arm joint from the steering knuckle, be careful not to damage the dust cover of the suspension arm joint.
The following bolts are pre-coated with friction stabilizer. If these bolts are reused, they may work loose.

s1.ptxt: Hoist vehicle and remove front wheel.
Remove engine undercover and engine under side covers.
Loosen suspension arm joint nut (1) until nut end becomes flush with stud end of suspension arm joint.
Disconnect suspension arm joint (1) from steering knuckle (2) using puller (3).

attention2.ptxt: Ball joint puller may fall off when suspension arm joint is disconnected and cause an injury.
Suspend the ball joint puller from the vehicle body using a rope to prevent the puller from falling off.

s1.ptxt: Remove suspension arm front bushing bolt (2) and front suspension frame bolt (3), and then remove suspension arm (1).
Install suspension arm (1) and tighten new suspension arm front bushing bolt (2) and new front suspension frame bolt (3) temporarily by hand.
Connect suspension arm joint to steering knuckle and then tighten suspension arm joint nut (1) to specified torque.

attention3.ptxt: If grease is stuck on taper surface of suspension arm joint and knuckle, remove it before connecting these parts.

s1.ptxt: Insert new clip (2) to suspension arm joint.
Install front wheel and tighten wheel nuts to specified torque.
Lower hoist and bounce vehicle up and down several times to stabilize suspension. Then, tighten suspension arm front bushing bolt (2) and front suspension frame bolt (3) to specified torque.
Hoist vehicle again, and then install engine undercover and engine under side covers.
Lower hoist, and then check front wheel alignment.
